blocks.task_summary: State the assumption made by setting L=200 in the logistic model.
method_path: State that the stable/long-term population will be the same as before the reduction.
accepted_alternatives: The maximum value / carrying capacity of the population will be 200.

evidence.basis: that the stable/long term population will be the same as before the reduction. A1 Note: Condone ‘the maximum value / carrying capacity of the population will be 200’.

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of C given x(0)=40 and L=200.
method_path: Substitute t=0, x=40, L=200 into logistic equation.
Solve 40 = 200/(1+C) to get C=4.

evidence.basis: attempt to substitute into logistic function (M1) 200/(1+Ce^0)=40 -> 40+40C=200 -> C=4 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of k given x(5)=70.
method_path: Substitute t=5, x=70, L=200, C=4 into logistic equation.

evidence.basis: correct substitution into their logistic function (A1) 70 = 200/(1+4e^{-5k}) -> k = 1/5 ln(130/280) ≈ 0.153 A1

blocks.task_summary: Predict wolf population at t=10 using logistic model, to nearest whole number.
method_path: Substitute t=10, L=200, C=4, k≈0.153451 into logistic equation.
Compute x ≈ 107.397...
Round to nearest whole number: 107.

evidence.basis: correct substitution into their logistic function (A1) x = 200/(1+4e^{-10*0.153451...}) = 107.397... -> x=107 A1

blocks.task_summary: Write down the value of dx/dt when x=200.
method_path: Substitute x=200 into dx/dt = a x ln(200/x) to get 0.

blocks.task_summary: Interpret dx/dt=0 at x=200 in context.
method_path: State that the population is steady/stable at 200, or this is the equilibrium population.
accepted_alternatives: The rate of change of wolf population is zero.

evidence.basis: the population is steady/stable (at 200) OR this (200) is the equilibrium population A1 Note: Accept phrases such as ‘the rate of change of wolf population is zero’. Do not accept 200 is the maximum.

blocks.task_summary: Show that f'(x) = 1/(x ln(200/x)) for f(x)=ln(ln200 - ln x).
method_path: Differentiate f(x)=ln(ln200 - ln x) using chain rule.
accepted_alternatives: Use f(x)=ln(ln(200/x)) and differentiate to get 1/(ln(200/x)) * (x/200)*(-200/x^2) = -1/(x ln(200/x)).

evidence.basis: EITHER 1/(ln200 - ln x) * (-1/x) M1 -> f'(x) = -1/(x ln(200/x)) A1 OR product of three expressions M1A1 -> AG

blocks.task_summary: Use separation of variables to show general solution ln x = ln 200 - A e^{-a t}.
method_path: Separate variables: 1/(x ln(200/x)) dx = -a dt.
Integrate both sides: ∫ 1/(x ln(200/x)) dx = ∫ -a dt.
Use result from (iii) to get ln(ln200 - ln x) = -a t + c.
Exponentiate: ln200 - ln x = e^{-a t + c} = A e^{-a t}.
Rearrange to ln x = ln200 - A e^{-a t}.
accepted_alternatives: Separate as 1/(x ln(200/x)) dx = a dt and integrate to get -ln(ln200 - ln x) = a t + c, leading to same result.

evidence.basis: attempt to separate variables M1; 1/(x ln(200/x)) dx = -a dt A1; ln(ln200 - ln x) = -a t + c A1A1; ln200 - ln x = e^{-a t + c} = A e^{-a t} A1; ln x = ln200 - A e^{-a t} AG

blocks.task_summary: Find A using x(0)=40, giving answer as A=ln p.
method_path: Substitute t=0, x=40 into ln x = ln200 - A e^{-a t}.
Solve ln40 = ln200 - A to get A = ln200 - ln40 = ln(200/40) = ln5.

evidence.basis: correct substitution ln40 = ln200 - A e^0 (A1) -> A = ln5 A1 (p=5)

method_path: Substitute t=5, x=70, A=ln5 into ln x = ln200 - A e^{-a t}.
Solve ln70 = ln200 - ln5 e^{-5a} to get a ≈ 0.0854528...
Round to 0.0855 (3 s.f.).

evidence.basis: correct substitution ln70 = ln200 - ln5 e^{-5a} A1; a = 0.0854528... A1; a = 0.0855 to 3 s.f. AG

blocks.task_summary: Predict wolf population at t=10 using Gompertz model, to nearest whole number.
method_path: Substitute t=10, a≈0.0854528, A=ln5 into ln x = ln200 - A e^{-a t}.
Exponentiate to get x ≈ 100.839...
Round to nearest whole number: 101.
accepted_alternatives: Using a=0.0855 gives x≈100.871..., rounded to 101.

evidence.basis: correct substitution (A1); 100.839… (A1); 101 to the nearest whole number A1

blocks.task_summary: Comment on the predictions made by the two models compared to actual population 85.
method_path: State that both models overestimate, or that the Gompertz model is closer to the true value.

evidence.basis: both are overestimates OR the Gompertz is closer to the true value A1

blocks.task_summary: Use Euler's method with step 0.5 from t=5, x0=70 to estimate population at t=10.
method_path: Set up Euler iteration: x_{n+1} = x_n + 0.5 * (0.0855 x_n ln(200/x_n) - 0.03 x_n).
Perform iterations from t=5 to t=10 with step 0.5.
Obtain final estimate x ≈ 89.42803...
Round to nearest whole number: 89.

evidence.basis: attempt to use Euler (M1); correct formula (A1); evidence of correct use (A1); after 10 years population 89 wolves (89.42803…) A1

blocks.task_summary: Comment on the Euler estimate compared to actual or other models.
method_path: Compare result to actual number of wolves or to other models, e.g., it is more accurate/realistic.

evidence.basis: correctly compare their result to the actual number of wolves or to the other models or both. A1
